title: Let him kiss me — drama reminder; historical vs spiritual
english: [[Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:2]]. We must remember what we warned in the preface: this little book, having the look of an epithalamium, is written in the manner of a drama. We said a drama is where certain persons are brought on who speak, and others sometimes come forward, others withdraw or approach, and so the whole is carried on in changes of persons. This, then, will be the form of the whole little book, and according to it a historical exposition will be fitted by us as we are able. But the spiritual understanding will, the Lord granting, be opened in what follows.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I earliest-forward after Prologus CLOSEOUT.

title: Kisses of his mouth — not one kiss but many
english: The Bride therefore prays and says: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth. She desires not one kiss but kisses. The kisses of the Word are illuminations and teachings by which the soul is touched. So long as kisses were sent through the prophets and the law, the kiss of the Bridegroom’s own mouth had not yet been given. But now the more perfect Bride desires that the Word himself be present to her and speak mouth to mouth, as was said to Moses.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I earliest-forward after Prologus CLOSEOUT.

title: Your breasts better than wine; fragrance of ointments
english: [[For your breasts are better than wine >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:2]]. The breasts of the Word are teaching that nourishes little ones with milk and the perfect with solid food. The letter of the law is compared to wine, which sometimes intoxicates toward the letter without the spirit. Christ’s breasts are better, because they bring grace and truth. [[The fragrance of your ointments is above all spices >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:3]]: the name of Christ and the fame of his preaching have filled the whole world with fragrance.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I earliest-forward after Prologus CLOSEOUT.

title: Your name is ointment poured out; young women love you
english: [[Your name is ointment poured out >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:3]]. The name of Jesus has been poured out everywhere. As ointment, when the alabaster is broken, fills the house, so Christ’s name, when preached in the world, has filled all things. [[Therefore the young women have loved you >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:3]] — beginning souls and churches that have newly believed, drawn by the fragrance of his name.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I earliest-forward after Prologus CLOSEOUT.

title: Draw me after you; the king brought me to his chambers
english: [[Draw me after you; we will run into the fragrance of your ointments >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]. The Bride asks to be drawn, because without the Word’s drawing she cannot run. [[The king has brought me into his chambers >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]: the secrets of wisdom and the mysteries of the Scriptures. Let us exult and rejoice in you: not in ourselves, but in the Bridegroom. Mindful of your breasts above wine: rightly do they love you.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I earliest-forward after Prologus CLOSEOUT.

title: I am black but beautiful, O daughters of Jerusalem
english: [[I am black but beautiful, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:5]]. Black because of penitence and struggles in the body; beautiful because of the image of God and conversion. The tents of Kedar are black; Solomon’s curtains are adorned. [[Do not look at me because I am dark, for the sun has discolored me >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:6]]: the sun of trials sometimes scorches the soul, but does not take away inner beauty.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I earliest-forward after Prologus CLOSEOUT.

title: My mother’s sons fought me; keeper of vineyards
english: [[My mother’s sons fought against me; they made me keeper of the vineyards; my own vineyard I have not kept >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:6]]. Mother’s sons: those who seem from the same synagogue or the same race persecuted the church — as Saul did. She was set as keeper of vineyards, that is of churches or souls; and while she keeps others, she sometimes neglects her own — not by fault of love of neighbor, but by the weight of care.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I earliest-forward after Prologus CLOSEOUT.

title: Tell me where you pasture at noon
english: [[Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you pasture, where you lie down at noon, lest I begin to wander after the flocks of your companions >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:7]]. Noon is full light and perfect knowledge. The Bride seeks the Word’s pastures not at evening or dawn but at noon. Without the Bridegroom’s showing she wanders among alien flocks — doctrines and sects.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I earliest-forward after Prologus CLOSEOUT.

title: If you do not know yourself — goats, not sheep
english: [[If you do not know yourself, O beautiful among women, go out and follow the tracks of the flocks, and pasture your goats beside the shepherds’ tents >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:8]]. Knowledge of oneself is the beginning of return to God. If the Bride does not know herself, she will pasture among goats — not sheep — and be separated from the Bridegroom. Beautiful among women: the church among souls, or the soul among virtues.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I earliest-forward after Prologus CLOSEOUT.

title: Likened to my cavalry; ornaments until the king reclines
english: [[I have likened you, my friend, to my cavalry among Pharaoh’s chariots >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:9]]. As far as the Lord’s cavalry differs from Pharaoh’s horses, so far the church differs from alien daughters. [[Your cheeks are beautiful as a turtledove’s; your neck as necklaces >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:10]]. [[We will make you ornaments of gold with studs of silver, until the king reclines >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:11-12]]. Angels and the Bridegroom’s friends prepare ornaments for a time; when the Bridegroom has risen from the passion, he himself will bestow perfect gold and silver.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I earliest-forward after Prologus CLOSEOUT.

title: Therefore the young women loved you
english: [[Therefore the young women have loved you >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:3]]. The young women are souls lately come to faith, drawn by the fragrance of Christ’s name to love the Bridegroom, yet not yet arrived at perfect charity. They have loved — not yet do they love perfectly in the present; it is promise and beginning. As far as the fragrance of the ointment reaches, so far the young women run; when the name has been emptied out in the passion, then they love more abundantly.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I CLOSEOUT at Song 1:4; Liber II opens Nigra sum.

title: Draw me after you; we will run
english: [[Draw me after you; we will run >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]. The Bride asks to be drawn, because [[no one comes to the Word unless the Father draws him >> Bible:John 6:44]]. She asks in the singular — draw me — and promises in the plural — we will run — because when one soul is drawn, many young women follow. [[Into the fragrance of your ointments >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]: they run not first by sight, but by the fragrance of fame and preaching, until they see face to face.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I CLOSEOUT at Song 1:4; Liber II opens Nigra sum.

title: The king brought me into his chambers
english: [[The king has brought me into his chambers >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]. The chambers are the secrets of wisdom, hidden treasuries of knowledge. King Christ brings the soul from outside to what is within, from letter to spirit, from history to mystery. We will exult and rejoice in you: joy not in the chambers themselves, but in the king who brings her in.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I CLOSEOUT at Song 1:4; Liber II opens Nigra sum.

title: Mindful of your breasts above wine; the upright love you
english: [[Mindful of your breasts above wine; rightly do they love you >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]. The breasts of the Word are better than the wine of the law. Those who are upright in heart, not perverse, love the Bridegroom. The wine of the letter sometimes intoxicates toward error; Christ’s breasts nourish toward life. Uprightness of heart is the measure of true love.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I CLOSEOUT at Song 1:4; Liber II opens Nigra sum.

title: Equity has loved you — charity without iniquity
english: [[Equity has loved you >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]. The young women say this as if making excuse, as though they do not yet perfectly love the breasts above wine. Equity is what loves Christ, because charity admits no iniquity. [[If you love me, keep my commandments >> Bible:John 14:15]]: whoever loves, keeps; whoever keeps, has equity. As much iniquity as is in us, so far are we from the love of Christ.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I CLOSEOUT at Song 1:4; Liber II opens Nigra sum.

title: Virtues love Christ; he is justice and peace
english: We can also take it thus: Equity has loved you — as if to say justice, truth, wisdom, chastity and each of the virtues have loved Christ. Nor is it strange: in other places Christ is usually taken as the substance of the virtues themselves. He himself is justice and peace and truth; and again these embrace him. [[Justice and peace have kissed >> Bible:Psalm 85:10]].
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I CLOSEOUT at Song 1:4; Liber II opens Nigra sum.

title: Same one as Bridegroom and Bride by economy
english: The same one is called Bridegroom and Bride, according to places and times. [[As a bridegroom he has set a mitre on me, and as a bride he has adorned me with ornament >> Bible:Isaiah 61:10]]. Christ fits his form to each cause: sometimes Bridegroom of the soul, sometimes Bride of the Father, sometimes wisdom that is sought, sometimes Word that seeks. Book I has set out these things concerning the kiss and the breasts and the name and the chambers and equity.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I CLOSEOUT at Song 1:4; Liber II opens Nigra sum.

title: Historical line of Book I gathered
english: The historical shape: the Bride — church or soul — prays that the Word present give kisses of teaching; she says the breasts of grace are better than the wine of the letter; Christ’s name, ointment poured out, gathers the young women; drawn, they run; they are brought into the chambers of the mysteries; at last equity loves perfectly. This is the historical line of the First Book.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I CLOSEOUT at Song 1:4; Liber II opens Nigra sum.

title: Spiritual sense of Book I gathered
english: The spiritual sense: the kiss is union of Word and soul; the breasts are the teachings of both Testaments; wine is the killing letter; ointment is the Spirit and the preaching of Jesus’ name; drawing is grace; chambers are contemplation; equity is purity of heart without iniquity. Whoever is not yet fit for these remains a young woman and follows the fragrance until she receives the perfect kiss.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I CLOSEOUT at Song 1:4; Liber II opens Nigra sum.

title: Liber I CLOSEOUT — toward Nigra sum
english: End of the First Book. In the following Book we shall pursue, the Lord granting, what is said: [[I am black and beautiful, O daughters of Jerusalem >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:5]]. Thus far, from Let him kiss me through Equity has loved you, as we were able, with Rufinus interpreting, we have expounded. Glory to you, Christ, Word and Bridegroom. Amen.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 33.
Liber I CLOSEOUT at Song 1:4; Liber II opens Nigra sum.
